researcher_notes:
Covered all 7 vendors. No usable raw material existed in restaurant_tech_research_2026-07-21.json's candidate_evidence array for any of these 7 (checked all 936 rows by 'Vendor Archive' key -- none matched grubbrr/toshiba/zivelo/olea/kiosk-information-systems/nextep/appetize), so all 12 records below came from fresh web research. Coverage is uneven: Grubbrr (4 records) and Zivelo (3) are the strongest vendors in this batch with clear dated multi-unit evidence; Nextep (2), Olea (2) and Appetize (1) are real but thin, mostly single-location/pilot-scale; Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions and KIOSK Information Systems came back with zero usable restaurant-specific evidence -- both vendors are overwhelmingly grocery/retail/healthcare case-study shops with only generic, unnamed 'QSR' marketing copy for foodservice. Confirmed no kiosk-specific NCR evidence beyond the NCR Voyix x GRUBBRR 'Aloha Kiosk' product partnership announced 2024-05-16 (PYMNTS) -- that is a vendor-to-vendor technology partnership (NCR + Grubbrr jointly building a kiosk product), not a NCR-to-restaurant-brand deployment, so no record was created for it; flagging it here for awareness only, not double-counting POS-category NCR work.

Three corporate-structure findings, two of which CORRECT premises stated in the task brief rather than confirm them: (1) Zivelo was acquired by Verifone on 2019-09-02 (confirmed via Kiosk Marketplace/Crunchbase) -- no longer independent, though the 'ZIVELO' sub-brand name persists in some 2020s case-study material ('ZIVELO, now part of Verifone'). (2) Nextep Systems was acquired by SICOM in June 2018, and SICOM was itself acquired by Global Payments for $415M later in 2018 and folded into Global Payments' Xenial platform -- Nextep's own site now brands itself 'NEXTEP SYSTEMS - Now a Part of Xenial.' This means Xenial (already listed in the POS Platforms category of the vendor universe draft as 'formerly Squirrel/HME/Panasonic') should also be understood to carry Nextep/SICOM lineage; flagging for the eventual Xenial entity write-up rather than creating a duplicate vendor line here. (3) Appetize: the task brief's premise that Appetize was acquired by Legends in 2022 could NOT be confirmed and appears to be incorrect -- no Legends-Appetize transaction exists in any source checked (Legends' 2023-2024 acquisition activity was of ASM Global, a venue-management company, unrelated to Appetize). What actually happened: SpotOn Transact acquired Appetize in 2021 for $415M; then Shift4 Payments acquired SpotOn's sports-and-entertainment division (which included Appetize) for ~$108.7M, closing 2023-10-02. Appetize is therefore now Shift4-owned, not Legends-owned -- worth noting Shift4 Payments already appears as its own vendor line in the Payments category, so there may be future convergence similar to the Global Payments/Worldpay situation flagged in that batch. (4) Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions: could NOT confirm the task brief's premise of a 2022 Sunny Optical joint venture/rebrand -- extensive searching found no such transaction. What IS confirmed: Toshiba Corporation itself was taken private via a JIP-led consortium tender offer, delisted from Tokyo Stock Exchange 2023-12-20; Toshiba Tec Corporation (TGCS's direct parent) remains a separate, still-Toshiba-affiliated entity; TGCS continues operating and publishing press releases under the 'Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions' / 'Toshiba Commerce' name as recently as EuroCIS 2025 and a November 2025 Merco grocery-chain case study. No rename or ownership change specific to TGCS was found -- Todd should treat the task brief's Sunny Optical claim as unconfirmed/likely mistaken rather than fact.

Failure mode called out in the task brief (pilot dressed up as rollout) was real and encountered repeatedly: Bojangles' November 2024 PR reads as a system-wide announcement but the actual quoted language is 'bring this technology to more of our locations in the coming months' with no committed unit count, so it's written as active_rollout rather than brand_wide_deployment. Several Olea and Nextep 'case studies' turned out to be unnamed ('one national QSR chain,' 'a prominent national sandwich chain' with a 200-store deployment and 24-week payback) -- excluded as unusable per the brief's instruction not to fabricate/guess a brand name.

records.confidence_rationale: Direct company press release plus on-record CIO quote (Richard Del Valle), corroborated by multiple independent trade-press outlets (Restaurant Dive, RestaurantNewsRelease.com).
records.notes: Follows a successful pilot (>50% kiosk adoption at some test locations). Announcement language is 'bring this technology to more of our locations in the coming months' -- no committed total unit count disclosed, so written as active_rollout rather than brand_wide_deployment despite Bojangles operating ~800-820 restaurants system-wide. Do not overclaim full-chain completion from this record alone.

records.confidence_rationale: Company press release with on-record CEO quote (Kep Sweeney), specific 3-phase rollout confirmed complete across all four states PDQ operates in.
records.notes: Samsung-hardware kiosks powered by Grubbrr software, rolled out across all PDQ locations in Florida, North Carolina, New York and New Jersey following an August 2023 pilot. 'All locations' here means all locations in PDQ's four operating states, not necessarily a larger national footprint -- PDQ itself only operates in these four states.

records.confidence_rationale: Official press release with specific pilot metrics (18.5% ticket-size lift, 75% of orders via kiosk) and named exclusive-vendor commitment; corroborated by fastcasual.com and AVNetwork trade coverage.
records.notes: Samsung Kiosk powered by Grubbrr. Deployed across all 17 of BurgerFi's corporate-owned Florida locations following a Dec 2021 pilot; franchise locations (the larger share of BurgerFi's ~100+ system) were offered an opt-in, not mandated. BurgerFi named Grubbrr its exclusive self-ordering technology provider. Written as significant_deployed_footprint rather than brand_wide/all_location because franchise adoption was optional, not confirmed system-wide.

records.confidence_rationale: On-record CTO quote (Leon Davoyan) in a dedicated trade-press feature, with specific unit-count and sales-mix figures.
records.notes: Kiosks live in almost 300 of the chain's ~440 global stores (~68%); ~25% of Dave's overall sales now flow through kiosks. Testing began 2024 partly in response to California's fast-food minimum-wage increase. Not confirmed as full/all-location deployment -- article explicitly frames it as an ongoing expansion, not yet complete.

records.confidence_rationale: Trade-press article (kioskindustry.org, covering a Zivelo/Dell OEM partnership announcement) quotes an on-record McDonald's USA statement confirming an ongoing multi-year relationship, but no official McDonald's or Zivelo press release with exact unit counts was located independently.
records.notes: Zivelo has supplied self-order kiosks to McDonald's USA since 2015, per a direct McDonald's USA quote: 'ZIVELO has been, and continues to be, a good business partner to McDonald's in our deployment of Self-Order Kiosks in the US.' No specific unit count disclosed in this source; McDonald's USA's broader kiosk rollout (thousands of restaurants) is well documented elsewhere but this specific source does not itself quantify Zivelo's share of that footprint, so written conservatively.

records.ai_application: AI-powered voice ordering assistant with a dynamic menu that adjusts by weather/time/season/location, built for drive-in/drive-thru ordering.
records.confidence_rationale: Joint Mastercard/Zivelo press release naming Sonic explicitly as the first pilot partner, with on-record Zivelo CEO quote.
records.notes: Explicitly described as a pilot at 'selected Sonic locations' -- exact location count not disclosed. This is drive-thru/voice-AI adjacent rather than a classic countertop self-order kiosk, but Zivelo is fundamentally a self-service kiosk hardware/software company and this was its own AI-kiosk innovation announcement, so kept in this category rather than the separate drive-thru/voice-AI batch (checked -- Zivelo/Sonic does not appear in phase2_drivethru_voiceai_evidence_draft_2026-08-03.json, so this is not a duplicate).

records.confidence_rationale: Detailed vendor case study (via Intuiface, Zivelo's software partner) with specific technology-stack detail, but not an official Zivelo or Thai Chili 2 Go press release, and exact publish date had to be corroborated from a related local-news article.
records.notes: Small regional fast-casual Thai chain, seven Arizona locations at the time. Case study explicitly labels the vendor 'ZIVELO (now part of Verifone),' independently corroborating the Verifone acquisition. Coverage is ambiguous on whether the kiosk software reached all seven locations or just the newest one (Gilbert Santan) at time of writing -- written conservatively as deployed_scope_not_publicly_disclosed rather than all_location_deployment.

records.confidence_rationale: Trade press (Kiosk Industry) with an on-record, named executive quote (Mike Repetti, then CIO/CDTO of Habit Burger Grill) describing an existing kiosk deployment, but no official Olea or Habit press release found, and location count is not disclosed.
records.notes: Article describes Habit Burger Grill's COVID-era adaptation of moving Olea 'Austin model' countertop kiosks outside for contactless ordering, implying kiosks were already an established part of Habit's in-store operations pre-pandemic, but does not state how many locations had them.

records.confidence_rationale: Official Olea press release with specific, dated deployment scope (2 of 200+ locations).
records.notes: Flagged as a borderline restaurant-category fit, similar to the Nala Robotics/Re-Up call in the Computer Vision batch: CEFCO is fundamentally a Texas-based convenience-store chain (200+ locations), and this deployment is specifically for its in-store 'CEFCO Kitchen' made-to-order foodservice concept, installed in only 2 Temple, TX locations at launch. Olea's kiosk is the 'Austin' model; software partner is Reji LLC.

records.confidence_rationale: Historical (2009) trade-press coverage (Hospitality Technology) naming the concept, location, and managing partner, but predates the deeper digital-press-archive era so cross-corroboration is thinner than for more recent records.
records.notes: Touch-screen ordering kiosks installed at Wow Bao's State & Lake location in Chicago (a Lettuce Entertain You Enterprises concept), single location, under new managing partner Geoff Alexander. No evidence found of a subsequent multi-unit Nextep rollout at Wow Bao -- a later (2022) large-scale Wow Bao kiosk/vending expansion used a different vendor (Automated Retail Technologies), not Nextep.

records.confidence_rationale: Multiple independent trade-press sources (Kiosk Marketplace, Fast Casual, QSR Magazine) corroborate the same franchisee name, location, and technology stack.
records.notes: Nextep kiosks (4 units) powered by Revel Systems POS, at a single all-digital/kiosk-only Moe's location in Pittsburgh's Oakland neighborhood, opened by multi-unit franchisee Mike Geiger near University of Pittsburgh/Carnegie Mellon. Explicitly a franchisee-driven single-location concept, not a Moe's Southwest Grill corporate brand standard -- a second planned kiosk-only location (Charlottesville, VA, different franchisee) was announced for Q1 2020 in the same coverage but not independently confirmed as opened.

records.confidence_rationale: Official PR Newswire press release with specific, dated rollout timeline and exact location count.
records.notes: Gourmet fast-casual soup chain, 20 restaurants across NYC, Long Island and Boston. Pilot began Oct 2020 at the Herald Square location; systematic rollout reached over half the chain by press-release date, with full chain-wide completion targeted end of January 2021. This is Appetize's full omnichannel suite (POS + self-service kiosks + handhelds), not a kiosk-only deployment -- written vendor_role as system_of_record_pos since it replaced Hale & Hearty's entire prior POS system, with self-service kiosks as one component of that suite. This was the only clearly-sourced restaurant-chain (as opposed to stadium/venue/institutional) record found for Appetize; see researcher_notes and vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence for why.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions -- extensive searching (press releases, trade press, own case-study pages) turned up zero dated, named restaurant/foodservice-chain customers. TGCS's public case studies are overwhelmingly grocery and general retail (Merco, Metcalfe's Market, Grupo El Rosado/Hipermarket El Dorado) plus some healthcare/DMV work; the company's own marketing references 'hospitality and food service' only in generic terms with no named chain attached.

KIOSK Information Systems (KIOSK.com / KIOSK Inc) -- similarly thin. Company markets itself heavily toward retail, healthcare (a Maryland MVA/DMV case study was the most concrete named example found), and general enterprise HR/manufacturing kiosks. Its own 'Restaurant Kiosks' product page and QSR-focused blog content contain no named chain customers or case studies, only generic industry statistics.
vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: Zivelo -- acquired by Verifone, announced 2019-09-02. No longer an independent company; Verifone integrated Zivelo's hardware designs into its own payment/POS/self-service line. The 'ZIVELO' name still appears in some post-acquisition case-study material (labeled 'now part of Verifone'), so treat as a sub-brand within Verifone rather than a fully retired name.

Nextep Systems -- acquired by SICOM Systems in June 2018; SICOM was itself acquired by Global Payments later in 2018 (~$415M) and merged into Global Payments' Xenial restaurant-technology platform. Nextep's own site now brands as 'NEXTEP SYSTEMS - Now a Part of Xenial.' Relevant cross-reference: Xenial already appears in the vendor universe draft's POS Platforms category (noted there as 'formerly Squirrel/HME/Panasonic') -- add Nextep/SICOM to that lineage note when Xenial is researched as its own vendor.

Appetize -- the task brief's stated premise (acquired by Legends in 2022) could not be confirmed and appears incorrect; no Legends-Appetize transaction was found anywhere. Actual chain of ownership: SpotOn Transact acquired Appetize in 2021 for $415M; Shift4 Payments then acquired SpotOn's sports-and-entertainment division (including Appetize) for ~$108.7M, closing 2023-10-02. Appetize is now Shift4-owned. Shift4 Payments already exists as its own vendor line in the Payments category of the vendor universe -- flag for possible future convergence/consolidation similar to the Global Payments/Worldpay note in that batch.
